alt: A grid of family size, birth rate, death rate, infant and child mortality and ageing, each with what has happened and its main explanations, plus internal and international migration.
caption: Each demographic change reshapes the structure of families.

alt: Left: an earlier family shape with few generations and many members in each. Right: a beanpole family of four generations with one or two members each and a pivot generation in the middle. Falling fertility and rising life expectancy produce the change.
caption: Lower fertility and longer lives make families long and thin.

alt: Three positions on families and industrialisation: Parsons and Goode’s functionalist fit, Laslett and Anderson’s historical challenge, and Young and Willmott’s stages ending in the symmetrical family, with a note on urbanisation.
caption: Households shrink in cities, but family networks often stay extended.

after: ## Family diversity: the named newer types
alt: A grid of pivot generation, reconstituted, living apart together, child-free and beanpole families with definitions and links to social change, and a note on laws such as divorce reform and China’s one-child policy.
caption: Each newer family type has a demographic, legal or cultural driver.

alt: Individualisation theorists Beck, Beck-Gernsheim and Giddens see relationships as freely chosen and fragile; Smart argues people stay embedded in webs of relationships and proposes personal life. Stacey’s divorce-extended family illustrates postmodern diversity.
caption: Smart: choices are real, but made within relationships and histories.

alt: A global care chain: a migrant woman cares for a richer family’s children abroad while her own children are cared for by relatives or paid help. Cards cover Parreñas on transnational families and families of choice, personal communities and pets.
caption: Care and family life now stretch across borders and beyond kin.

alt: A five-step plan for a 20-mark essay on demographic causes of family diversity: introduction, arguments for, arguments against, application to a named society and a conclusion.
caption: Demography sets the conditions; laws and culture decide the forms.
